name: Primary Cutaneous Marginal Zone B-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of dense, nodular or diffuse infiltrate of small B-cells with marginal zone differentiation in the dermis and subcutis
B-cell markers positive (CD20+, CD79a+), negative for CD5, CD10, and cyclin D1
Solitary or multiple erythematous to violaceous papules, plaques, or nodules localized to the skin without extracutaneous involvement at diagnosis
Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement supporting monoclonality

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of marginal zone B-cell infiltrate with appropriate immunophenotyping and clinical presentation localized to the skin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of systemic lymphoma and other cutaneous B-cell lymphomas is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythematous to violaceous cutaneous papules or plaques
Solitary or multiple slowly growing skin nodules

searchTerms: skin feels thick and firm in one spot
episodes of skin redness and swelling

occasional.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating
immune system attacks related to cancer

laboratory: Monoclonal B-cell population detected by flow cytometry
imaging: PET-CT or CT scan showing skin-limited disease without systemic involvement
Ultrasound of regional lymph nodes to exclude extracutaneous spread
genetic: Clonal immunoglobulin heavy chain gene rearrangement
Absence of t(11;18)(q21;q21) translocation typical of other MALT lymphomas
other: Histopathology demonstrating marginal zone B-cell infiltrate with plasma cell differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a; negative for CD5, CD10, cyclin D1

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents with solitary or grouped plaques or nodules on head or trunk
Lack of clonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangement
Often associated with preceding infection or inflammation

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of extracutaneous dissemination on imaging
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Grange F, Beylot-Barry M, Beylot C. Primary cutaneous marginal zone B-cell lymphoma: clinical and histopathologic features and treatment. Dermatol Clin. 2015;33(4):619-628.
Orphanet: Primary cutaneous marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. ORPHA178536.
